blocks.html: Transitioning from a monolithic architecture to a microservices architecture introduces multiple operational challenges.
blocks.text: Transitioning from a monolithic architecture to a microservices architecture introduces multiple operational challenges.

blocks.html: Each microservice must individually handle authentication, authorization, and other repeated concerns.
blocks.text: Each microservice must individually handle authentication, authorization, and other repeated concerns.

blocks.html: These duplicated responsibilities increase complexity and reduce efficiency across services.
blocks.text: These duplicated responsibilities increase complexity and reduce efficiency across services.

blocks.html: To simplify this, an intermediary layer is placed between the clients and the microservices.
blocks.text: To simplify this, an intermediary layer is placed between the clients and the microservices.

blocks.html: This layer, called an API Gateway, acts as the central entry point for all client requests.
blocks.text: This layer, called an API Gateway, acts as the central entry point for all client requests.

blocks.html: The API Gateway offloads shared responsibilities, allowing microservices to concentrate solely on their core business logic.
blocks.text: The API Gateway offloads shared responsibilities, allowing microservices to concentrate solely on their core business logic.

blocks.html: TLS (Transport Layer Security) Enforcement & Termination
blocks.text: TLS (Transport Layer Security) Enforcement & Termination

blocks.html: The API Gateway enforces encryption by accepting only encrypted traffic (mainly HTTPS) and rejecting all unencrypted (HTTP) requests.
blocks.text: The API Gateway enforces encryption by accepting only encrypted traffic (mainly HTTPS) and rejecting all unencrypted (HTTP) requests.

blocks.html: The gateway then performs TLS termination, where it decrypts the incoming encrypted data.
blocks.text: The gateway then performs TLS termination, where it decrypts the incoming encrypted data.

blocks.html: After decryption, the gateway can inspect, validate, and route requests to internal services.
blocks.text: After decryption, the gateway can inspect, validate, and route requests to internal services.

blocks.html: This ensures that external communication stays secure, while internal routing and processing can happen efficiently as the internal services would not have to bother about decryption.
blocks.text: This ensures that external communication stays secure, while internal routing and processing can happen efficiently as the internal services would not have to bother about decryption.

blocks.html: Rate Limiting
blocks.text: Rate Limiting

blocks.html: Defines a fixed maximum number of requests a client can make within a specific time window (e.g., 100 requests per minute).
blocks.text: Defines a fixed maximum number of requests a client can make within a specific time window (e.g., 100 requests per minute).

blocks.html: Once the limit is reached, the gateway rejects further requests (usually with HTTP status 429 – Too Many Requests).
blocks.text: Once the limit is reached, the gateway rejects further requests (usually with HTTP status 429 – Too Many Requests).

blocks.html: Ensures fair usage among clients and prevents denial-of-service (DoS) attacks.
blocks.text: Ensures fair usage among clients and prevents denial-of-service (DoS) attacks.

blocks.html: Throttling
blocks.text: Throttling

blocks.html: Instead of rejecting excess requests outright (as in Rate Limiting), it slows down request processing.
blocks.text: Instead of rejecting excess requests outright (as in Rate Limiting), it slows down request processing.

blocks.html: Can queue, delay, or degrade service when limits are exceeded.
blocks.text: Can queue, delay, or degrade service when limits are exceeded.

blocks.html: Useful for graceful degradation — preventing system crash under heavy load.
blocks.text: Useful for graceful degradation — preventing system crash under heavy load.

blocks.html: Often combined with rate limiting to handle temporary spikes more smoothly.
blocks.text: Often combined with rate limiting to handle temporary spikes more smoothly.

blocks.html: Throttling: Soft control — excess requests are delayed or slowed down.

blocks.html: Aggregation
blocks.text: Aggregation

blocks.html: Backends are often structured so clients can fetch all required data with minimal requests.
blocks.text: Backends are often structured so clients can fetch all required data with minimal requests.

blocks.html: When a single client operation needs data from multiple microservices, an aggregated endpoint is created at the API Gateway.
blocks.text: When a single client operation needs data from multiple microservices, an aggregated endpoint is created at the API Gateway.

blocks.html: The API Gateway breaks that aggregated request into multiple internal calls, gathers the responses, merges them, and returns a unified result to the client.
blocks.text: The API Gateway breaks that aggregated request into multiple internal calls, gathers the responses, merges them, and returns a unified result to the client.

blocks.html: Advantages
blocks.text: Advantages

blocks.html: It enables centralized security management for the system perimeter.
blocks.text: It enables centralized security management for the system perimeter.

blocks.html: It achieves reduced coupling because the client implementation does not need to worry about the backend architecture.
blocks.text: It achieves reduced coupling because the client implementation does not need to worry about the backend architecture.

blocks.html: It improves fault tolerance of the overall system.
blocks.text: It improves fault tolerance of the overall system.

blocks.html: There are many ways, one way is that, in case if the microservices fails to respond, it can internally retry.
blocks.text: There are many ways, one way is that, in case if the microservices fails to respond, it can internally retry.

blocks.html: It can improve performance through aggregation, reducing client chattiness and latency.
blocks.text: It can improve performance through aggregation, reducing client chattiness and latency.

blocks.html: It allows scaling up internal services more easily.

blocks.html: It is highly complex to operate and requires continuous updates against new market attacks.

blocks.html: It can be costly to implement.
